biography.plain_text: Sam Spiegel was an American film producer who built his fortune through independent filmmaking. Born in Galicia, then part of Austria-Hungary, he co-founded Horizon Pictures with John Huston. His productions On the Waterfront, The Bridge on the River Kwai and Lawrence of Arabia each won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

long_biography.plain_text:
To obtain the rights to The African Queen, film producer Sam Spiegel secured a loan from a sound-equipment supplier. With Humphrey Bogart and Katharine Hepburn committed to starring, he then arranged American financing and exchanged European distribution rights for the sterling needed for production.

His art collection encompassed Impressionist and early modern paintings, sculpture and works on paper, including pieces by Monet, Matisse and Picasso. After his death, much of the collection went to the Israel Museum. Film royalties from his estate also supported practical training at the Jerusalem film school that bears his name.
